mara: If you're here for a sword, you're out of luck.

choice.text: I need to reach the bell tower.
Lovely to see you too, Mara.

mara: Rowan? Orin's apprentice? You've grown. Not much. Upwards, mostly.
I need to reach the bell tower.
Then you're even more out of luck.
The old mechanism broke. Orin asked me to repair it, then vanished.
Anything made of iron can be fixed.
It's the things made of promises you have to worry about.
Here. This is what he wanted looked at.
The bell's tuning pin. My family's made and mended it since before the chapel had a roof.
It's sound. Not a crack in it. Whatever broke up there, it wasn't this.
Have a look, if you like. There's a worn patch near the head. My father used to rub it with his thumb when he was thinking.
The pin's on the bench. Go on. It won't bite. Probably.
Find anything? You've got Orin's habit of staring at things until they confess.
He used to put his ear to that worn patch. Swore it talked. Daft old man.

mara.text: (Stand close to the pin and press F to listen.)

mara: Alden's at the chapel, east of the square. He'll want to see that pin. Don't let him keep it.
You've got the look of someone who learned something they'd rather not have.

choice.text: The bell takes memories. Yours too.

mara: So that's where it went. The song.
Every night I wondered why I could still feel the weight of him, and not hear it.
Go on, then. Up the road. And Rowan... whatever you decide up there, decide it like someone who'll have to live with it.
Fair. Some things should be said once, and properly. Mind the road north.
Go on. I'll keep the forge hot. Somebody in this village should be good at keeping things.
mara_marks: There's a symbol on the pin. A bell surrounded by thirteen marks.
Thirteen? My father told me the bell only rings twelve times.
Lately, there are a lot of things I don't remember.
Not like this. Not the things that matter.
I used to sing to my boy. Every night, when he was small. He's grown now. Works the river barges.
I remember the weight of him. The smell of his hair. The way he fought sleep like it owed him money.
But the song I sang him... it's gone. Like a page torn out. I can feel the edge where it was.
Ask him why I can remember holding my boy as a baby, but not the song I sang to him.
Don't promise things in this village, Rowan. They have a way of getting lost.
Honest. Orin always said you were honest to a fault. Mostly the fault.
If you want to know what that bell really is, ask Brother Alden at the chapel. His books are older than my anvil.
forge_pin: An iron pin, long as a forearm, heavy and cold. Generations of hands have worn it smooth.
There's a worn patch near the head. Something was engraved here once.

forge_pin.text: Some things remember more than they show. (Stand close and press F to listen.)

forge_pin: The marking has faded again. But I know what I saw. Mara should hear about this.
forge_pin_echo: For a moment the iron is warm, and the worn patch fills with pale light.
A bell. And around it... thirteen marks.
forge_plaque: A board above the hearth, carved in old letters:
BRANNOC. IRON FOR THE BELL. FIRE FOR THE VILLAGE.
Mara's family. They've kept the bell longer than anyone's kept anything.
forge_swords: Three swords on a rack. Each one has a tag: NOT FOR SALE.
The middle one's tag says: ESPECIALLY NOT FOR SALE.
forge_barrel: The quenching barrel. Water, soot, and what you sincerely hope is a sausage.
forge_jar: A jar labelled CURSES. It is very nearly full.
A smaller jar beside it is labelled APOLOGIES. It contains a single, lonely button.
forge_cradle: A small wooden cradle, worn smooth at the rockers. These days it holds kindling.
She kept it. Of course she kept it.
forge_cradle_echo: The forge fades. A younger Mara sits beside the cradle, rocking it with one boot, humming.
There's no tune. Just the shape where a tune should be. Like the notes were scraped off.
forge_furnace: The furnace breathes like a sleeping dragon. Your eyebrows have opinions about standing this close.

forge_anvil.text: Touch my anvil and I'll mend you next.
An anvil scarred by a thousand days of work. It hums faintly under your hand.
